memo.verdict: Park, not progress. Neutral at EUR 11.9 (28 September 2026); conviction: working hypothesis. Azelis is a cause-for-concern clearing in a solid but leveraged specialty distributor, coherent rather than compelling: the shares at EUR 11.9 already pay for the clearing that has happened (customers finished destocking, supplier price rises passing through, EUR 20m of cost out) and for little of the clearing that has not (leverage back inside 3.0x). The modal return is 20.2 percent a year over eighteen months (a 31.8 percent total) and 14.5 percent a year over three years (50.3 percent total), against the framework's 20 percent bar; the eighteen-month figure rests on a re-rating at near-even odds, the earnings path compounds at 9.2 percent a year (below the 12 to 20 percent band), and the drop-through sensitivity takes the eighteen-month return to 7.9 percent a year at the blended multiple and below zero at the uncleared one. The park rule is not triggered (management C, business quality C, predictability C, trackability C); the case is parked on the return, not on a gate. Triggers to progress with a bullish direction: a price below about EUR 10.4, where both horizons clear the bar on the modal path; or a Q3 2026 update (late October 2026) showing organic growth of 3 percent or more with volume named as the driver and the working-capital build unwinding, which would lift the cleared-branch odds from 45 percent toward 60 percent and the eighteen-month return into the middle of the B band at the same price. Trigger to bearish: a Q3 2026 update with organic growth below 2 percent or with price named as the driver, which would show the concern is not clearing and would invalidate rather than park.
case: - The concern was three things at once, all in the share-price history: three years of destocking-led organic decline (-5.9 percent 2023, -1.1 percent 2024, -1.6 percent 2025, -3.9 percent Q1 2026); a leverage overshoot to 3.4x against a 2.5x to 3.0x target that stopped an acquisition engine of 64 deals in 8.5 years; and three consecutive years of sell-side downgrades. Together they took the shares to EUR 6.7231 and the multiple to 7.0x EV to EBITDA in January 2026.

- The change is mostly external and partly temporary. Destocking has ended: Q2 2026 group organic growth +3.9 percent against consensus 1.8 percent after four quarters of decline, corroborated by IMCD's +7.5 percent in the same quarter, so the end of destocking is a sector fact. Suppliers announced price increases of up to 30 to 40 percent on selected portfolios in H1 2026 and customers largely accepted them, lifting the gross margin 100 basis points to 24.7 percent; management itself expects the pricing and inventory benefits to ease in H2 2026. The company's own cycle (KQ 6, RA 1, E 1, BB 1) and the supply side (KQ 5) are the two B forces; macro (KQ 7) is a D headwind (EMEA 45.5 percent of revenue; EMEA Life Sciences -6.6 percent organic in H1 2026; the euro).

- The internal change is discipline, not transformation: a EUR 20m run-rate cost programme delivered ahead of plan (EUR 21m in 2025, EUR 6m in Q1 2026, EUR 11m in H1 2026), a refinancing saving EUR 6.5m a year from March 2026, ANZ pruning (20 percent of APAC revenue), a new chief financial officer, a guidance step for FY2026 from flat to positive adjusted EBITA growth on 30 July 2026. The three pillars are unchanged, the IPO targets (8 to 10 percent revenue growth, 10 to 15 basis points of margin a year) were abandoned in mid-2023, acquisition spend fell from EUR 585m in FY2023 to EUR 230m in FY2025, the dividend is flat at EUR 0.226, buybacks are EUR 1.5m of incentive cover. Three internal forces rate B (standards improvement, price rises, other leaders); none is strong in the screen's sense. Red flags: no false positive found.
counter_case: At its strongest: the Q2 2026 inflection is the final pricing gasp of a multi-year destocking cycle, not a volume recovery, and the shares are a value trap. The 30 to 40 percent supplier price increases and two to three months of low-cost inventory produced the 100 basis point gross margin gain and the 46.0 percent conversion margin, a jump of the kind that reverts. Industrial Chemicals' Q2 growth of 4.2 percent was predominantly pricing rather than volume. EMEA Life Sciences fell 6.6 percent organically in H1 2026 and the European long tail of SME manufacturers that justifies the high-touch model is shrinking. A Middle East de-escalation reverses the pricing, as Deutsche Bank warns. Working capital absorbed EUR 29m of free cash flow in the half, free cash flow fell 19 percent, and leverage rose to 3.4x. Brenntag was downgraded in June 2026 on the same pricing peak. The sell-side's ratings never capitulated (75 percent Overweight and zero Underweight in late 2025; seven Buy and six Hold today), so the fourth year of downgrades has room to run once H2 2026 disappoints. The Risks report's own analysis of competing hypotheses gave this false-friend profile the win with two disconfirming items against nine. On this reading the shares, 77 percent off the low, have re-rated to a level that leaves no room for the disappointment. And Morgan Stanley's consensus for FY2026 organic growth was 0.7 percent before the results, the recovery is hand-to-mouth with 8 to 10 weeks of visibility, and the company does not disclose volume, so the pricing-illusion reading cannot be disproved from the accounts.

At the foundations: the exclusive-mandate model becomes obsolete as Western principals lose global share to non-exclusive Chinese producers; Azelis's early embrace of Chinese sourcing in 2024 infuriated Western principals, who pulled existing mandates, so the moat erodes from the supplier side while the customer side shrinks; Chinese principals are under 10 percent of European portfolios but structurally expanding; the EMEA gross margin, the early-warning series, has not been reported by region and so cannot be shown to be holding.
triggers: - The decisive open question: whether Q2 2026 organic growth was volume or price. The company does not disclose the split; the Q3 2026 trading update in late October 2026 tests whether organic growth holds at 3 to 4 percent once the inventory benefit reverses. Growth of 3 percent or more with volume named and the working-capital build unwinding lifts cleared-branch odds from 45 percent toward 60 percent and moves the recommendation to progress, bullish, at the same price. Growth below 2 percent, or growth with price named as the driver, moves it to bearish and invalidates: the disruption-abating condition of the primary setup fails and the return falls to an F on the sensitivity path.

- The second open question: whether leverage returns inside 3.0x during 2027. Year-end 2026 leverage at or below 3.1x on the company's basis moves the cleared branch toward probable; above 3.4x toward unlikely. Alarm above 3.4x at December 2026 or net working capital above 15 percent of revenue; invalidate above 3.8x including deferred payments. The chief financial officer has declined to give a landing date.

- The third: whether the pricing pass-through holds the gross margin at 24 percent or better through 2027 (plausible, about 50 percent). Alarm below 24.0 percent; invalidate below 23.5 percent for two consecutive quarters. A Middle East de-escalation is the reversal route.
- The fourth: whether the below-EBITA drop-through delivers (probable, about 70 percent): H2 2026 net financial expense above EUR 62m (H1 2026 was EUR 66m) would change the view.

- The fifth: which earnings line the market prices. Likely the upper cluster but unverifiable from the inputs; price targets from the Buy houses that reconcile to the lower cluster (about EUR 0.70 for FY2027) would change the view and would mean the re-rating leg is already spent.
- Price trigger: below about EUR 10.4 both horizons clear the 20 percent bar on the modal path, and the recommendation moves to progress with a bullish direction.
